static_traits.name: Zhu Lian
static_traits.medical_history: Has not received psychotherapy or psychological intervention in the past; without significant physical illness.
static_traits.language_features: High cooperation, clear expression, self-observation ability; tone slightly tense but positive attitude, open, able to describe triggering situations and emotions logically.

basic_info.main_problem: I have a tendency to label myself negatively and personalize small mistakes, leading me to feel I am useless. These not-good-enough feelings have existed since I can remember, and are more obvious recently. The initial stress was lighter, possibly triggered by a shopping mistake. The problem has developed to the point where I keep giving myself negative labels for tiny mistakes, affecting self-esteem. I have these feelings every time I make a mistake, especially when shopping. I try to remind myself that everyone makes mistakes, but the negative feelings remain.
basic_info.core_demands: I have noticed that persistent negative self-labeling affects my emotions and self-perception, so I hope to reduce this negative pattern and improve my self-understanding through counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not capable in any aspect of life

special_situations.event: Forgetting to use the rewards card / points when checking out at the supermarket (a small mistake in a shopping situation)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a small mistake while shopping, it means I am a useless shopper, and I do not do anything well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to soothe myself with 'everyone makes mistakes', but with poor effect; then engaging in harsh self-criticism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a useless shopper; I cannot do anything well

special_situations.event: Making a recipe mistake while cooking at home (a small slip in a household situation)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do every small thing right, it means I am overall not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses harsh self-evaluation to push himself to avoid making mistakes again

special_situations.event: Minor social faux pas in social settings (small mistakes in social situations)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake in social situations, others will look down on me and think I am stupid
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding talking with close friends about my negative labeling pattern, digesting anxiety alone
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am stupid; I have disappointed everyone again

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted, and to see himself as valuable and capable
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being negated and looked down on because of small mistakes, being evaluated overall as 'incompetent'
defense_goal: Through harsh self-criticism and self-labeling, preemptively controls and guards against external evaluation, so as to gain a 'sense of control' over mistakes

object_relations.self_representation: Incompetent, a failure who easily messes things up
object_relations.object_representation: People who will criticize, look down on, and negate me for small mistakes

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking in counseling about shopping or small mistakes in life, or when invited to observe and record present emotions and thoughts
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating small mistakes with overall incompetence, believing mistakes will lead others to negate oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Self-blaming tone, using absolutist language (such as 'always', 'completely'), emphasizing one's own faults and devaluing self-worth.

manifestations: Not yet discussing my negative self-labeling pattern with close friends
outcomes: Experiencing a stronger sense of isolation and self-denial after making mistakes

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently using self-blaming and absolutist statements when describing mistakes (such as 'I always mess things up')
Restricts self-expression and support-seeking with harsh self-evaluation

positive_force: Positive help-seeking attitude, willing to try behavioral experiments and collect data
Has the willingness and ability for self-observation and recording
Has a close friend to confide in (a potential support resource)
negative_force: Habitual negative self-labeling, overgeneralization, and personalization
Impaired self-esteem, mood swings, overreacting to small mistakes
Avoiding discussing my own patterns with friends, leading to insufficient use of social support

target_behavior.behavior: Negative self-labeling and harsh self-criticism after small errors
antecedent: Forgetting to use the rewards card when checking out while shopping
Minor social blunder in a social setting
target_behavior.core_reason: The deep belief equating small mistakes with overall incompetence, accompanied by the cognitive distortions of overgeneralization and personalization
target_behavior.function: Briefly relieving uncertainty and anxiety through self-criticism, trying to gain a 'sense of control' over mistakes through self-punishment
target_behavior.consequence: Lowered self-esteem, low mood, friendships becoming strained, affecting daily activities and self-feelings
